metadata.title: Claim Maintenance: a specification for the continuous, independent observation of public claims (version 0.2)

creators.name: Templeman, Nicholas
creators.affiliation: Council of AI (CSOAI Ltd), United Kingdom

metadata.description:
Version 0.2 of the Claim Maintenance specification. It supersedes version 0.1 (10.5281/zenodo.22901908), which keeps its bytes.

What changed. The version 0.1 reference extractor departed from section 6.3 step 2 in four ways. It did not decode hexadecimal character references, it decoded only five named references, it decoded &... twice, and it threw on a decimal reference above U+10FFFF. The text of section 6.3 is unchanged. Version 0.2 adds source_content_hash.extractor (section 5.6.1) so that a visible-text digest names the extractor that produced it. It adds section 6.3.1, under which digests are compared only like with like and a change of extractor is re-baselined, never recorded as an observed change. The reference implementation uses csoai-visible-text/2 and keeps csoai-visible-text/1 unchanged, so every version 0.1 digest still recomputes. Section 16 lists the changes.

Claim maintenance is not fact-checking, not auditing, not reputation scoring and not adversarial journalism, and it issues no mark. It asserts no falsity about anyone.
metadata.notes: Measurement only. This specification issues no mark and defines no body that grants one. UNMEASURED and UNCHECKABLE are first-class states and are published as prominently as measured ones. The reference implementation is MIT; the document is CC0.

files_note: sha256 values are of the bytes on branch claims/extractor-decode-once-20260925 when this file was written. The register snapshot carries an as_of and changes on every regeneration; re-hash it at upload time and record what was uploaded. The document of record's sha256 is what deposit.json must carry.
does_not_prove: that the specification is endorsed by Zenodo, CERN or anyone else; a repository deposit is storage and an identifier, not a review
that the specification is correct; a DOI makes a document citable and permanent, not right
